before: The typical symptoms of GERD are heartburn and regurgitation of stomach contents up into the throat or mouth [1].
GERD happens when stomach contents flow back up into the esophagus or mouth, causing symptoms or complications [1].

The condition is most effectively treated with proton-pump inhibitors, though long-term use of these medications carries risks including bone fractures, kidney disease, pneumonia, and intestinal infection [1].
